as_told.title: Sheehan defends Mack before the Harvard faculty committee

plain: John Mack was a psychiatrist and professor at Harvard University who took the UFO subject seriously. According to Lue Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who ran a small office studying unexplained aerial reports, Harvard tried to get rid of Mack, and Mack went to court and won. Whitley Strieber, an author who says he has met non-human beings himself, tells it a bit differently. He says Mack was invited to a meeting that turned out to be an ambush, aimed at taking away his licence to practise psychiatry. A lawyer, Dan Sheehan, tells it first-hand. He says that when Mack was confronted by a faculty committee, Mack called him and asked him to be his lawyer. The tellers differ on whether it was a court case or a committee hearing. If true, it would show a top university punishing a respected scholar for studying the subject.
